intent: A captioned section of options in a SelectContent, named for assistive technology by the SelectLabel inside it.
typical_uses: A labelled section of a long option list, such as the regions of one continent

dont_use_when.situation: A visual break between options with no caption

invariants.text: The group renders `role="group"` and takes its accessible name from the SelectLabel inside it, through `aria-labelledby`, unless the caller passes its own `aria-labelledby`; a group with neither has no name.
select.module.css gives the group no padding and no divider; the list pads every option the same whether or not a group encloses it.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the group's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the group's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (an empty object for a group). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through select.module.css, not through this.

good.title: Two captioned sections divided by a rule

bad.title: A group with no caption, used only to wrap the options
bad.why: The group adds no spacing and, without a SelectLabel, no name; it only announces an unnamed group. Place the items straight under SelectContent.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, SelectGroupState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the group's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: SelectGroupState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function of the group's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (an empty object for a group). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through select.module.css, not through this.
